42858632.label: Purpose
42858632.text: To evaluate the diagnostic performance and interreader agreement of the Clear Cell Likelihood Score (ccLS), the modified Clear Cell Likelihood Score (m-ccLS), and ancillary MRI features for differentiating benign from malignant renal masses and clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) from non-ccRCC lesions.

42858632.label: Materials and methods
42858632.text: This retrospective single-center study included 106 patients with renal masses who underwent multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) between 2018 and 2026. MRI features, including T1 signal intensity (SI) ratio, T2 SI ratio, apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) ratio, and arterial-to-delayed enhancement ratio (ADER), were evaluated. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis in both the overall cohort and the cT1a subgroup. Two radiologists independently assigned ccLS and m-ccLS scores and assessed the presence of a pseudocapsule for interreader agreement analysis.

42858632.label: Results
42858632.text: Among 106 renal masses, 73 (68.9 %) were classified as cT1a tumors. For differentiating benign from malignant renal masses, m-ccLS demonstrated higher diagnostic performance than ccLS in both the overall cohort (AUC, 0.770 vs. 0.654) and the cT1a subgroup (AUC, 0.784 vs. 0.689). For differentiating ccRCC from non-ccRCC lesions, ccLS and m-ccLS showed comparable diagnostic performance in both the overall cohort (AUC, 0.884 vs. 0.868) and the cT1a subgroup (AUC, 0.885 vs. 0.876). Among the evaluated ancillary MRI features, the T2 SI ratio was significantly associated with both benign-malignant discrimination and ccRCC identification. Interreader agreement for ccLS, m-ccLS, and pseudocapsule assessment was substantial.

42858632.label: Conclusion
42858632.text: Incorporation of pseudocapsule assessment into the ccLS improved differentiation between benign and malignant renal masses while maintaining comparable diagnostic performance for identifying ccRCC. T2 SI ratio may provide additional value in MRI-based characterization of renal masses.

42897082.label: Background
42897082.text: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides accurate anatomical assessment of coronary stenosis severity but has limited ability to determine lesion-specific ischemia as assessed by invasive fractional flow reserve (FFR). We aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of an artificial intelligence-based deep learning CCTA-derived FFR model (CT-FFRAI) in cohorts undergoing CCTA and invasive FFR as part of a study protocol and a real-world cohort undergoing invasive FFR based on suspected coronary artery disease on CCTA in routine clinical care.

42897082.label: Materials and methods
42897082.text: Diagnostic performance of CT-FFRAI (CorEx, SPIMED-AI) was evaluated using an intention-to-diagnose approach and compared with CCTA using 50% and 70% stenosis thresholds, with invasive FFR as reference standard. In the PACIFIC-1 study cohort, 208 patients underwent CCTA and invasive FFR assessment of all major coronary vessels irrespective of CCTA findings. The real-world cohort included 202 patients with at least one CCTA-defined lesion ≥70% stenosis who underwent ICA with invasive FFR.

42897082.label: Results
42897082.text: In the PACIFIC-1 cohort (612 vessels), per-vessel diagnostic accuracy was comparable between CT-FFRAI (77%), when using a CCTA based ≥50% stenosis threshold (76%; P = 0.689), and when using a ≥70% stenosis threshold (74%; P = 0.183). In the real-world cohort (325 vessels), CT-FFRAI demonstrated higher per-vessel diagnostic accuracy (63%) compared with CCTA using ≥50% and ≥70% stenosis thresholds (52% and 57%, respectively; P < 0.001 and P = 0.034). Net reclassification improvement for CT-FFRAI beyond CCTA alone using ≥50% and ≥70% stenosis thresholds was 7.9% (P = 0.256) and 17.7% (P = 0.012) in the PACIFIC-1 cohort, compared with 23.2% (P < 0.001) and 13.6% (P = 0.070) in the real-world cohort, respectively.

42897082.label: Conclusions
42897082.text: CT-FFRAI may outperform anatomic assessment alone, with diagnostic accuracy depending on the prevalence of obstructive coronary artery disease and the range of stenosis severities among vessels undergoing invasive FFR assessment.

42900382.label: Purpose
42900382.text: Esophageal variceal (EV) bleeding is a lethal complication in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Current risk stratification relies on invasive endoscopy or systemic surrogates of liver cirrhosis. This study aimed to develop a machine learning model utilizing EV-specific CT radiomics to identify high-risk esophageal varices, as defined by endoscopic criteria, in patients with HCC.

42900382.label: Methods
42900382.text: 151 HCC patients were enrolled and divided into a training cohort (n = 101; 75 high-risk; January 2017 - December 2022) and an independent temporal validation cohort (n = 50; 29 high-risk; January 2023 - December 2024). Endoscopic stigmata were used as an endpoint, including active bleeding or varices with high-risk features. Radiomic features were extracted from contrast-enhanced CT images acquired within six months prior to endoscopy. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC) of receiver operating characteristic (ROC), Brier score, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA).

42900382.label: Results
42900382.text: In the training cohort, the varix-specific radiomics signature developed via the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) demonstrated excellent discriminative power (cross-validated AUC: 0.956; 95% CI 0.872-1.000). In the temporal validation cohort, this model maintained high generalizability, yielding an AUC of 0.926 (95% CI 0.846-0.984, sensitivity: 93.1%, specificity: 71.4%) as well as a Brier score of 0.1186 and good calibration (intercept = -0.157, slope = 1.354). Surface-to-Volume Ratio (SVR) and NGTDM Coarseness are feasible radiomics.

42900382.label: Conclusion
42900382.text: The varix-specific radiomics model provides highly sensitive and mathematically stable non-invasive risk stratification for EV bleeding in patients with HCC.

42986432.label: Background
42986432.text: Early-stage liver fibrosis is reversible; thus, accurate staging of liver fibrosis is of great importance. Liver biopsy is the gold standard for the diagnosis of liver fibrosis; however, its invasive nature limits its clinical application. Accurate noninvasive staging of liver fibrosis remains challenging. Thus, there is an urgent need for a precise and reliable noninvasive diagnostic approach.

42986432.label: Objectives
42986432.text: A topological deep learning model combining topological data analysis and EfficientViT framework (TopoEfficientViT) was developed to effectively capture global contextual relationships in hepatobiliary phase MR images for assessment of staging liver fibrosis.

42986432.label: Methods
42986432.text: Our retrospective study included patients with chronic liver diseases from June 2018 to July 2025, which was approved by our Institutional Review Board. Our data from a hospital site (Site A) in our institution were divided into a training set (n = 275) and a validation set (n = 75). The test set (n=65) was composed of data from a separate hospital site (Site B) in the same institution.

42986432.label: Results
42986432.text: A total of 415 patients (323 males, mean age 56.52±9.54 years; 92 females, mean age 58.86±9.68 years) were enrolled in the study. In the training set, the AUC and accuracy of TopoEfficientViT for staging liver fibrosis F1-2 vs. F3-4 were 0.942 and 0.906, respectively; for staging liver fibrosis F1-3 vs. F4 were 0.957 and 0.891, respectively. In the validation set, the AUC and accuracy for staging liver fibrosis F1-2 vs. F3-4 were 0.849 and 0.76, respectively; for staging liver fibrosis F1-3 vs. F4 were 0.861and 0.813, respectively. In the test set, the AUC and accuracy for staging liver fibrosis F1-2 vs. F3-4 were 0.829 and 0.769, respectively; for staging liver fibrosis F1-3 vs. F4 were 0.791 and 0.785, respectively.

42986432.label: Conclusion
42986432.text: The TopoEfficientViT model had high predictive performance for staging liver fibrosis by integrating multi-scale persistent homology topology with convolutional networks.

43007582.label: Background
43007582.text: Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) with [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE is increasingly applied for advanced gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NETs). This study aimed to characterize the development of hematologic parameters under PRRT in a large single-center cohort. We retrospectively analyzed 178 patients with GEP-NETs treated with [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE at a university hospital (2012-2023). Hemoglobin (Hb), white blood cell count (WBC), and platelet count (PLT) were assessed at baseline, after 2 cycles (FU1), after 4 cycles (FU2), during post-therapy follow-up (FU3), and at the last available timepoint (FU4). Patients with deteriorating blood values during or after therapy were categorized according to CTCAE v6.0. The occurrence of myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) within the period from completion of the initial PRRT to initiation of salvage chemotherapy or PRRT was investigated.

43007582.label: Results
43007582.text: Baseline mean values were Hb, 13.6 ± 1.6 g/dL; WBC, 6.9 ± 2.0 × 10⁹/L; and PLT, 256 ± 92 × 10⁹/L. A significant decline in those hematological parameters was observed at FU1 and FU2 (p < 0.01). Between FU2 and FU3, values recovered significantly (p < 0.001), with no further relevant change at FU4 for Hb and PLT, while WBC increased significantly compared to FU3. At last follow-up (FU4), all parameters remained significantly below baseline (all p < 0.001), but exhibited final values in a normal laboratory range (Hb, 12.4 ± 1.9 g/dL; WBC, 6.3 ± 2.6 × 10⁹/L; and PLT, 216 ± 78 × 10⁹/L). Based on CTCAE v6.0, only 4 patients (2%) developed grade 3 hematological adverse events and no grade 4 adverse event was observed. After completing four cycles of PRRT, 2 patients (1.3%) developed MDS according to the WHO criteria. Patients with chemotherapy prior to PRRT (n = 30) had lower baseline WBC and showed smaller on-treatment declines, but were the only subgroup without Hb recovery from the nadir (median change FU2 to FU4, - 0.35 vs. +0.35 g/dL; adjusted p = 0.017).

43007582.label: Conclusion
43007582.text: PRRT with [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE induces a mild short to midterm decline in hematologic parameters, which is followed by a significant increase during long-term follow-up, eventually returning to values within the laboratory reference range. Serious adverse events or MDS are very rare, supporting long-term overall hematologic safety.

43043182.text: Background Histotripsy recently received U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) clearance for liver tumors, but long-term safety data remain limited. Purpose To characterize histotripsy-related adverse events (AEs) reported to the Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience (MAUDE) database during the early postmarket period and contextualize findings in comparison to microwave ablation (MWA) and radiofrequency ablation (RFA) during comparable observation windows. Materials and Methods A retrospective analysis of the FDA MAUDE database was conducted. AE reports were analyzed over comparable 24-month postmarket periods: July 2024 to July 2026 for histotripsy, January 2017 to January 2019 for MWA, and January 2016 to January 2018 for RFA. Reports were classified by severity (malfunction, serious injury, and death) and medical problem category. Firth-penalized reporting odds ratios (RORs), relative risks (RRs), and Bayesian modeling using Bass model-derived procedure volumes enabled exploratory denominator-adjusted comparisons. Results Of 570 AE reports initially identified, 506 met the inclusion criteria and were included in the final analysis (71 histotripsy [median patient age, 68 years; IQR, 56-76 years] and 435 MWA/RFA [median patient age, 58 years; IQR, 50-67 years]). Serious injury and death occurred in 86% (61 of 71) and 14% (10 of 71) of histotripsy reports versus 20% (89 of 435) and 2% (eight of 435) of MWA/RFA reports. Histotripsy had higher reported odds of serious injury (ROR, 14.24 [95% CI: 6.29, 35.56]; P < .001) and death (ROR, 4.35 [95% CI: 1.08, 24.35]; P = .04). In exploratory analyses using modeled procedure volumes, estimated RRs based on reported events were 6.11 (95% CI: 2.64, 14.11; P < .001) for serious injury and 10.94 (95% CI: 4.73, 25.33; P < .001) for death. Although sparse event counts produced imprecise estimates for some complication categories, histotripsy showed higher reporting odds of renal and urinary complications (P < .001), hemorrhage and vascular injury (P < .001), and gastrointestinal and/or abdominal complications (P < .001) in the full cohort. A sensitivity analysis excluding malfunction-only reports showed similar organ system reporting patterns. Conclusion Histotripsy demonstrated higher reported frequencies of serious AEs and death in early postmarket MAUDE surveillance compared with pooled MWA/RFA; however, differences in technology maturity and reporting era may have contributed to differential AE reporting, warranting prospective evaluation.

43084432.text: Breast cancer treatment has progressively evolved toward less invasive, more personalized therapeutic strategies that maintain oncologic efficacy while minimizing morbidity. Cryoablation, a percutaneous image-guided technique, has emerged as a promising alternative to surgery in selected patients with breast cancer. Initially explored in patients unfit for surgery or those declining operative management, cryoablation is now supported by growing evidence demonstrating favorable local control rates for older women with low-risk, early-stage breast cancer. Ongoing trials are further investigating these findings and evaluating whether cryoablation may exert immunomodulatory effects that enhance systemic antitumor immunity. If so, this may provide a rationale for combination strategies with immune checkpoint inhibitors and cancer vaccines. The authors examine the technical principles of cryoablation, summarize clinical outcomes from key studies, and explore its role in special populations including elderly patients and those declining surgery. Ongoing research will determine how cryoablation can be integrated into standard breast cancer treatment as part of a broader movement toward therapeutic de-escalation.

43086482.label: Objective
43086482.text: Liver transplantation (LT) is an important treatment modality for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but recurrence after LT remains a major challenge with limited therapeutic options. Although yttrium-90 (Y-90) transarterial radioembolization (TARE) is now widely used for HCC, data on its efficacy in recurrent HCC after LT-particularly with resin microspheres-remain scarce. This study aimed to investigate the safety and efficacy of resin microsphere‑based TARE in patients with recurrent HCC following LT.

43086482.label: Methods
43086482.text: Consecutive patients with recurrent HCC after LT who underwent Y-90 TARE using resin microsphere between August 2022 and August 2026 at two Chinese centers were retrospectively enrolled. Tumor response was assessed using localized and overall modified Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (mRECIST). The main outcomes assessed were overall survival (OS) from TARE; additional outcomes included progression-free survival (PFS), objective response rate (ORR), adverse events (AEs), and prognostic factors. Kaplan-Meier method, log-rank test, and univariate Cox proportional-hazards regression were used.

43086482.label: Results
43086482.text: Twelve patients (1 female, 11 males; median age 60.5 years) were included. At recurrence, 91.7% (11/12) had multifocal lesions, 75.0% (9/12) had bilobar involvement, and 41.7% (5/12) had extrahepatic metastasis. The best localized ORR was 50.0% (6/12; 95% CI 21.1-78.9%), with 1 patient (8.3%) achieving complete response (CR), 5 (41.7%) achieving partial response (PR), and 5 (41.7%) having stable disease (SD); 1 patient (8.3%) was not evaluable (NE). No grade 3-4 adverse events occurred within 1 month after TARE; grade 1-2 events occurred in 33.3% (4/12). Median OS and PFS following Y‑90 TARE were 10.0 months (95% CI, 5.0-12.0) and 5.7 months (95% CI, 1.8-6.8), respectively. Local responders (CR + PR) had longer OS than non-responders (SD + NE, 11.0 vs. 5.7 months; P = 0.032). Tumor absorbed dose ≥ 100 Gy was likewise associated with longer OS (11.0 vs. 5.7 months; P = 0.023). In exploratory univariate Cox regression analysis, local tumor response (HR = 0.20, 95% CI, 0.04‑1.02, P = 0.052) and higher tumor absorbed dose (HR = 0.10, 95% CI, 0.01-1.05, P = 0.055) showed borderline protective effects.

43086482.label: Conclusion
43086482.text: Resin‑microsphere Y-90 TARE achieved favorable local tumor control with acceptable safety in patients with recurrent HCC after LT. Localized mRECIST-defined response and higher tumor absorbed dose were associated with improved survival. These exploratory findings require validation in larger multicenter cohorts.
